tasks.title: Typed read/write layer over the repo as a datastore

contract.inputs: A fine-grained GitHub PAT and the set of project repos it serves (owner/name), supplied through the config module. Callers name a repo and one of the three state documents.
contract.outputs: packages/state exports typed read and write functions for state/tasks.json, state/claims.json and state/users.json. Reads return a parsed, validated document. Writes accept a mutation function and commit the result.
invariants: Write path is: GET blob and sha, mutate in memory, PUT with that sha. On a 409, re-read and re-apply the mutation exactly once, then throw.
Every write is validated against the zod schema before any network call. A document that fails validation never reaches GitHub.
Reads are cached for 30 seconds.
The zod schemas agree with state/schema/*.json — same required fields, same patterns, same enum values.
Node 22, ESM, TypeScript strict. No use of `any`.

The client is repo-parameterised. Three project repos are served by one process — darwin-model, wildplaces and nostia-landing-redesign — so a repo is an argument, never a module-level constant, and the 30s read cache is keyed by repo AND document.
must_not_break: state/schema/*.json stays the canonical shape; the zod schemas mirror it and never diverge from it unilaterally.
tools/validate-state.js must still pass on any state this library writes.

The repo root stays CommonJS — no "type": "module" in the root package.json. tools/validate-state.js is CommonJS and the daily routine invokes it with a bare `node tools/validate-state.js`; adding a root type field breaks the routine's only safety gate. packages/state declares its own package.json with "type": "module".

open_decisions: Whether the write API takes a mutation callback (read-modify-write in one call) or exposes read and write separately and leaves the sha juggling to the caller.
Whether the 30s read cache is per-process in-memory or written to disk, and whether a write invalidates the cache for other documents or only its own.
How a 409 that persists after the single retry is surfaced — a typed error the bot can catch and report, or a plain throw.

tasks.title: Discord /task command with claim collision detection

contract.inputs: A Discord slash command /task project:<name> from a user in state/users.json, handled by discord.js v14 on top of packages/state. The project option is required and offers the configured repos as choices.
contract.outputs: Within the named project, picks the first task where state is open, every id in depends_on is merged, and touched_paths does not glob-intersect any active claim IN THAT PROJECT. Writes the claim, opens a thread, and posts the contract, the open_decisions list, the issue link and the branch name task/<id>. /board shows every configured project by default, grouped, and accepts an optional project filter.
invariants: Refuses if the caller already holds a claim, or is not in state/users.json.
Glob intersection agrees with tools/validate-state.js — in particular src/panel/** must be treated as overlapping src/panel/foo.ts.
No LLM call anywhere in the bot.
Two users racing /task cannot both be given overlapping tasks.
A user holds at most one claim across ALL projects, not one per project. Collision detection is per-project, because two repos cannot share a file path.
must_not_break: state/claims.json stays schema-valid after every command.
A failed claim leaves no partial state — no orphan thread, no half-written claim.

open_decisions: Whether the race between two simultaneous /task calls is prevented by an in-process queue, by relying on the 409 retry in packages/state, or by an advisory lock document in the repo.
Whether 'first task' means lowest id, oldest issue, or fewest dependents, when several are eligible.
Whether the glob matcher is copied from tools/validate-state.js, imported from a new shared package, or reimplemented against the same test table.

tasks.title: Integration harness plus one worked end-to-end example

contract.inputs: The composed system as it stands on main, exercised through real user paths rather than unit seams.
contract.outputs: tests/integration/ with a runner and exactly one fully worked example test that a human can read as a template for the rest.
invariants: Tests exercise composed behaviour, not single functions in isolation.
The suite runs against main with one command and reports pass or fail without a human reading the output.
No test depends on live Discord or a real PAT; anything external is faked at the boundary.
must_not_break: .github/workflows/pr.yml keeps running only tests/smoke on pull requests — integration runs nightly, not per PR.
The diff guard that stops contributors editing tests/ stays in force.

open_decisions: Which runner — node:test, vitest, or a hand-rolled script — weighing zero-dependency operation against ergonomics.
Where the boundary fake lives: an injected transport, a local HTTP stub, or recorded fixtures replayed from disk.
Whether the nightly workflow opens one rolling issue labelled integration-break and reuses it, or a fresh issue per failing night.

tasks.title: Bicep and OIDC deploy workflow for the bot on Azure Container Apps

contract.inputs: The bot's container image built from packages/bot's Dockerfile (from t-002), and Azure subscription/resource-group values supplied as GitHub Actions repository variables and OIDC federated credentials — no stored secret.
contract.outputs: deploy/ containing a Bicep template that provisions an Azure Container App (min replicas 1, no ingress, outbound websocket only) reading the Discord token and GitHub PAT from Key Vault, plus .github/workflows/deploy.yml that builds and pushes the image and runs `az deployment group create` against that template on every push to main that changes packages/bot/** or deploy/**.
invariants: Authentication to Azure is via OIDC federated credentials (azure/login with no client secret); no service principal secret is stored in GitHub or in the repo.
The Container App is provisioned with minReplicas 1 and no external ingress, matching the outbound-only websocket connection the bot needs.
Discord token and GitHub PAT are read from Key Vault at deploy time; neither value appears in the workflow YAML or in deploy/ in plaintext.
must_not_break: packages/bot/** stays the only place the bot's application code and Dockerfile live; deploy/ contains only infrastructure definitions.
.github/workflows/pr.yml keeps running on pull_request only; deploy.yml must trigger on push to main, never on pull_request, since it needs write credentials.

open_decisions: Whether the workflow rebuilds and pushes the image on every push to main regardless of which files changed, or only when packages/bot/** or deploy/ changes — simplicity versus wasted deploys.

Whether Key Vault references are wired into the Container App as environment variables synced by Bicep, or mounted as a secret volume via the Key Vault CSI-equivalent — different blast radius if a value rotates.

Whether the container registry is Azure Container Registry provisioned by this same Bicep template, or an existing registry referenced by name — owning more infrastructure versus depending on a manual prerequisite.

tasks.title: Stale-claim report tool for the evening /verify pass

contract.inputs: state/claims.json and state/tasks.json, read directly from disk with no npm dependency, plus an optional --days flag (default 3).
contract.outputs: tools/stale-claims.js: a CLI script that prints each claim whose claimed_at is older than the threshold, alongside its task id and title, in a format /verify's report step can read or paste directly.
invariants: Runs with a bare `node tools/stale-claims.js`, no npm install, consistent with the rest of tools/** staying dependency-free.
Age is computed from claimed_at in UTC, compared against the current time, using the same RFC3339 parsing the claims schema documents.
Exits 0 whether or not any stale claims are found; exit code reflects a script error, not the presence of stale claims.
must_not_break: tools/validate-state.js remains the only script state writers must pass before committing; this tool never writes state.
state/schema/claims.json and state/schema/task.json stay the source of truth for field names this script reads.

open_decisions: Whether staleness is judged purely by claimed_at age, or also checks for an open PR referencing the task (via `gh pr list`) and only flags claims with neither — more useful, but adds a network call and a `gh` dependency to a tool that has had none.

Whether output is a human-readable table for pasting into /verify's report, or JSON for a future consumer to parse — human-first is simpler now but forces a rewrite if something automates on top of it later.
Whether the --days threshold is a CLI flag, an environment variable, or hardcoded to match the '~3 days' the runbook and /verify already mention informally.

tasks.title: CI check that a PR's diff stays inside its task's touched_paths

contract.inputs: A pull request's diff (`git diff --name-only` between base and head) and the task it claims to implement, found the same way /verify finds it: a `Task: t-XXX` line in the PR body, falling back to the task/t-XXX branch name.
contract.outputs: A new job in .github/workflows/pr.yml that looks up that task's touched_paths in state/tasks.json (read from the base ref, since the guard job already forbids editing state/ in the PR) and fails the check with the offending file names if any changed file falls outside every listed glob.
invariants: Uses the same glob-intersection semantics as tools/validate-state.js — a file matches a directory glob like packages/bot/** — so a false failure never blocks a legitimately in-scope change.
The task lookup logic matches .claude/commands/verify.md's own rule: prefer the Task: t-XXX body line, fall back to the task/t-XXX branch name, and treat a PR that matches neither as suspect.
The job reads state/tasks.json only from the base branch's ref, never from the PR head, since a PR is forbidden from editing state/ anyway.
must_not_break: The existing guard job in .github/workflows/pr.yml keeps failing any PR that edits state/ or tests/, independent of this new job.
PR body text is passed through env, never interpolated directly into a shell command, matching the existing decisions job's handling of attacker-controlled input.

open_decisions: Whether the glob matcher is copied from tools/validate-state.js's self-contained function, or that function is exported and required directly from the workflow's script step — duplication versus a new implicit dependency between tools/ and .github/.
Whether a PR that names no task fails this new job outright, or only warns and lets the existing 'What I decided' check be the hard gate for that case.
Whether an out-of-scope file fails the whole job immediately, or the job lists every offending file across the diff before failing, to save the contributor a round trip.

tasks.title: Serverless HTTP interactions endpoint, replacing the gateway bot

contract.inputs: Discord interaction POSTs, each signed with Ed25519 and carrying a timestamp header, delivered to a public HTTPS endpoint instead of arriving over a gateway websocket.
contract.outputs: packages/bot serves the same four commands from a request handler with no long-lived process. Signature verification, a deferred acknowledgement inside Discord's 3-second deadline, and a follow-up edit once the GitHub work finishes.
invariants: Every request is Ed25519-verified against the application public key before anything else happens. An unverified or replayed request is answered 401 and does nothing.
A PING (type 1) is answered with a PONG (type 1). Discord sends one to validate the endpoint and will not save it otherwise.
Commands acknowledge with a deferred response immediately and edit the original message when the work completes, because reading three GitHub repos does not fit in 3 seconds.
eligibility.ts, service.ts and format.ts are untouched. The hosting model is a shell concern; if a claim rule has to change to make this work, the seam was wrong.
No Node-only APIs on the request path — no Buffer, no node:crypto — so the same handler runs on a worker runtime and under Node.
must_not_break: The claim rules and their tests. Two users still cannot claim overlapping tasks, and one person still holds one claim across all projects.
packages/state stays the only code that talks to GitHub.

open_decisions: Whether to keep the discord.js gateway entry alongside the HTTP one for local development, or delete it. Two runtimes drift; one runtime means local testing needs a tunnel.

Where the follow-up work runs after the deferred acknowledgement — waitUntil on the worker platform, or a queue. waitUntil is far simpler and bounded by the platform's CPU limit, which a three-repo read may or may not fit inside.
Whether to drop @octokit/rest for plain fetch in packages/state. Octokit is a large dependency for two API calls and its Node assumptions are what force compatibility flags on a worker runtime.
